text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Hafez al-Assad holds talks with Lebanese parliament speaker Nebih Berri on developments in the region, the Middle East peace process and issues of common interest.
- European envoy Miguel Engel moratinos stresses that the Syrian-Lebanese tracks in peace moves are inseparable.
- Under directions from President Assad, Syria sends humanitarian aid to the Iranian areas hit by quakes.
- Syrian Prime Minister Mahmoud Zu'bi and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara discuss with Armenian foreign minister bilateral ties and the situation in central asia.
- Syrians in the Golan confirm belonging to Syria and take pride in the leadership of Assad.
- Syrian cabinet discuss ways to protect the archeological sites and the rights of depositors with money-collectors.
- In a stormy session of the Jordanian parliament, representatives demand ties with Israel be cut.
- Syria agrees with a British company to buy 14.300 tonnes of white sugar.
- France says the formula of the EU envoy Moratinos does not cancel the land-for-peace principle.
- Signs of a new Palestinian uprising loom and Israel confiscates 6000 acres of Jerusalem's lands.
- Syrian Vice-President Mohamed Zuheir Masharqa says Syria wants peace that preserves the dignity of everybody.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu meets mafia leaders and drug dealers in Russia before meeting President Boris Yeltsin and sharp difference over Jewish settlements in Jerusalem rise.
- Syria allocates 2.275 billion Syrian pounds in roads projects.
